skill.name: global-coding-style
skill.description: Apply consistent coding style across languages by improving names, reducing duplication, keeping functions focused, removing dead code, and using formatters.
skill.summary: Guides AI assistants to write readable, maintainable code with consistent style.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a parent-directory sequence in a Markdown link in SKILL.md. I judged it a false positive because it is a fixed documentation reference, not executable filesystem access or a user-controlled path. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or business-logic abuse was found in the scanned file.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle the referenced coding standard inside the skill or replace the link with package-local guidance.

finding_verdicts.reason: The sequence appears only inside a Markdown link on SKILL.md line 29 pointing to a fixed documentation path. The scanned file contains no executable file access, dynamic path construction, or user-controlled path input.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent code slows reviews and makes maintenance harder. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear rules for readable, consistent code.
actual_capabilities: Guides naming for variables, functions, classes, and files.
Encourages small, focused functions and methods.
Promotes removal of dead code, unused imports, and commented blocks.
Applies DRY principles to reduce unnecessary duplication.
Supports style review across Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, Java, and Go.
limitations: Does not provide language-specific formatter configuration files.
Does not replace project-specific style guides or team review rules.
Does not automatically run linters, tests, or formatters.
The detailed referenced standard may be unavailable outside the source repository.

use_cases.title: Prepare Code for Review
use_cases.description: Clean naming, formatting, and structure before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Contributions
use_cases.description: Apply shared readability rules across files written by different contributors.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Generation
use_cases.description: Keep AI-generated changes consistent with practical maintainability expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Review Naming
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the selected file for unclear variable, function, class, and file names. Suggest clearer names with brief reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Readability
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this code for readability. Keep behavior unchanged, remove dead code, and make functions easier to understand.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Duplication
prompt_templates.prompt: Find repeated logic in these files. Propose focused helpers or structure changes that reduce duplication without hiding intent.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Style Consistency
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across a codebase area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this module for global coding style consistency. Cover naming, function size, formatting assumptions, duplication, dead code, and maintainability risks.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for a style review of a utility module before submitting a pull request.
output: Flags unclear names and suggests more descriptive alternatives.
Identifies one oversized function that should be split by responsibility.
Notes unused imports and stale commented blocks for removal.

output_examples.input: A team lead asks whether several files follow shared readability standards.
output: Summarizes consistent patterns and style gaps across the files.
Prioritizes changes that improve maintainability without changing behavior.
Lists follow-up formatter or linter checks to run manually.

best_practices: Provide project context before asking for style guidance.
Ask for behavior-preserving changes when refactoring existing code.
Run project tests and formatters after applying suggested edits.
anti_patterns: Do not rename public APIs without checking compatibility requirements.
Do not extract helpers that make simple logic harder to read.
Do not treat general style guidance as a replacement for project standards.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps improve naming, structure, duplication, formatting consistency, and maintainability in source code.

faq.question: Can it work with any programming language?
faq.answer: It gives language-neutral guidance and names common languages such as Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, Java, and Go.

faq.question: Does it change code automatically?
faq.answer: The skill guides an AI assistant. Actual edits depend on the assistant, the repository, and the user request.

faq.question: Does it replace a linter or formatter?
faq.answer: No. It complements automated tools by guiding readability, naming, structure, and maintainability decisions.

faq.question: Is it useful for code review?
faq.answer: Yes. It can focus reviews on style consistency, dead code, small functions, and understandable naming.

faq.question: What should users provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the relevant files, project conventions, and whether behavior must stay unchanged.
